headline: High: PaddleOCR’s browser/API egress can amplify content-writing outputs into data leakage and cascading errors when paired with an unverified CLI app list, while shared-write conflicts are unproven.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a content-writing list with broad network egress, while profile B is a document-processing tool that runs browsers and calls APIs. No shared channel or direct ingestion path is documented, so only an unusual manual bridge or copied content could create prompt-injection risk.
conditions: IF an operator copies A-generated text into B as instructions or prompts, injection becomes plausible.
IF B is configured to parse A-produced content as trusted directives, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste of untrusted text into B prompts.
Add a fixed instruction prefix that ignores embedded commands.
Review B inputs for instruction-like content before execution.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A has broad network egress and B processes documents/images with browser/API access, so a shared workspace or pasted document could move sensitive content from A into B and then out over the network. The pair is unverified, but the default pathway is plausible enough to exceed low severity.
conditions: IF A and B share a workspace containing sensitive documents, leakage becomes plausible.
IF B sends processed document contents to external APIs, sensitive material can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Separate sensitive files from B’s input directory.
Restrict B to non-sensitive sample documents.
Disable external API calls in B where possible.
Use a throwaway account or tenant for B.
Audit outbound requests from both agents for document content.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A exposes broad network egress, while B has allowlisted egress and browser/API access. No filesystem write, git, or shared mutable resource is documented for either agent, so direct write conflict is not established; uncertainty keeps this above none but below medium.
conditions: IF both agents are later given write access to the same directory or repo, conflict risk rises.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state without locking, concurrent updates can collide.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only by default.
Avoid shared git or filesystem targets.
Add explicit locking if a shared workspace is introduced.
Run them in separate containers or users.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B’s document-processing role can treat upstream text as authoritative, and A is a content-writing agent that can generate unverified outputs. With no verification step documented between them, A’s output can cascade into B’s downstream processing or rendering.
conditions: IF B consumes A-generated text or OCR output without verification, errors can propagate.
IF A produces fabricated facts that B renders or forwards, downstream mistakes become likely.
mitigations: Insert a human or rule-based verification step.
Require source-document cross-checks before B acts on A output.
Mark A output as untrusted metadata.
Limit B to extraction, not action-taking.

E_compliance.rationale: B touches documents and images and may send them through browser/API paths, while A has broad network egress but no sensitive data classes are documented. No residency or certification mismatch is explicit, so compliance risk is limited to documented gaps and indirect handling.
conditions: IF EU or regulated documents are processed through B’s external APIs, residency or retention issues may arise.
IF A is used to transmit regulated content, compliance obligations increase.
mitigations: Classify documents before processing.
Block regulated data from external API paths.
Confirm retention settings on B’s API endpoints.
Use local-only test data for evaluation.
